title: Tool Use Reduces Depth-Induced Collapse in OOD Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2602.21061v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Many current paths to more advanced AI depend on the assumption that large language models (LLMs) can generalize learned relationships to solve complex, out-of-distribution (OOD) problems. However, this is not an easy quality to measure. For most real-world problems and benchmarks it suffices to exploit a few memorized subproblems or a small fraction of the available data to produce a correct solution. This is interpolation. Generalization requires the capacity to make use of all available data to solve problems without these shortcuts. To test this quality, we introduce a synthetic Boolean circuit reconstruction benchmark over $GF(2)$. We use an adversarial sampling oracle to block partial-information shortcuts, ensuring that each step requires the integration of all historical context with new evidence. translated_title: 工具使用减少OOD推理中的深度诱导崩溃
translated_abstract: arXiv:2602.21061v2 公告类型：替换。摘要：当前通向更先进人工智能的许多路径都依赖于这样一个假设：大语言模型（LLM）能够将学到的关系泛化，以解决复杂的分布外（OOD）问题。然而，这种能力并不容易衡量。对于大多数现实世界的问题和基准测试，只需利用少数记忆的子问题或一小部分可用数据即可产生正确答案——这是插值。而泛化要求模型具备在不借助这些捷径的情况下，利用全部可用数据来解决问题的能力。为测试这一能力，我们引入了一个基于 $GF(2)$ 的合成布尔电路重建基准，并使用对抗性采样预言机来阻断部分信息捷径，确保每一步都需要将全部历史上下文与新证据进行整合。我们的评估表明，独立的LLM在持续推理方面存在明显不足：随着问题深度的增加，小型模型……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于GF(2)的布尔电路重建基准，通过对抗性采样阻断部分信息捷径，发现独立LLM的推理能力会随问题深度增加而崩溃，而工具的使用可以缓解这种OOD推理中的深度诱导崩溃。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces a GF(2)-based Boolean circuit reconstruction benchmark with adversarial sampling to block partial-information shortcuts, showing that standalone LLMs collapse as problem depth increases, while tool use mitigates this depth-induced collapse in OOD reasoning.
